passage: Zainab, nineteen months old, heard the doorbell and pressed her face into her mother's leg. Pooja bent down, lifted her onto her lap and stayed relaxed and chatty as the neighbour came in. Zainab stared at the visitor with wide eyes, clutching Pooja's dupatta. No one pushed her for a hug. Ten minutes later, seeing her mother laughing easily, Zainab peeked out, gave a tiny wave and held out her toy rabbit. "Thank you, Zainab," the neighbour said quietly, without reaching for her, and Pooja smiled. Later Akash arrived and stretched out his arms. "Come, give uncle a kiss! Come, I will lift you up!" Zainab shook her head and turned away. Akash laughed. "Look at her acting shy!" and tried again. Zainab's lip trembled. Pooja said politely, "She doesn't feel like it today. Zainab, would you like to wave, or say namaste?" Zainab pressed her palms together and gave him a small namaste.

qa.q: What toy did Zainab hold out to the neighbour?
qa.a: She held out her toy rabbit.

qa.q: How did Zainab's behaviour with the neighbour differ from her behaviour when Akash asked for a kiss, and what did Pooja do each time?
qa.a: With the neighbour she hid and stared, then peeked, waved and offered her rabbit at her own pace once Pooja looked relaxed; with Akash, who pushed and laughed, she shook her head and her lip trembled, so Pooja backed her and offered a wave or namaste.

qa.q: What was Zainab probably feeling when Akash laughed at her refusal?
qa.a: She was uneasy and upset, since her lip trembled and she turned away, as if her no did not count.

qa.q: What could Pooja do the next time a relative pushes for a kiss?
qa.a: She could keep politely backing Zainab and offering a wave or namaste instead, without forcing any contact.

grounding: One toddler shows fear of a visitor, curiosity once her mother is at ease, and a relative who ignores her refusal until her mother backs her.
